standards_review.notes: code-review-final.json claimed '5 of 13 commits use conventional format instead of EPMCDME-XXXX:'. `git log main..HEAD --oneline` on this branch now shows 14 commits; only 2 (dc52bbe33, fd2be1109) match the 'EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence' pattern and the other 12 lack a ticket prefix entirely (not just wrong format) — so the original count was itself inaccurate. More importantly, .ai-run/guides/standards/git-workflow.md states this repo uses squash-merge: 'Each feature branch becomes one commit on main. The squash commit subject should follow the same EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence format.' The Tekton commit-format regex gate therefore applies to the single squash-merge commit set at merge time, not to every intermediate commit on the feature branch. Intermediate commit wording does not block CI and is not a legitimate review blocker.
No code-quality.md guide exists in .ai-run/guides/, consistent with the prior review's own note.

finding_notes.CR-016: Checked src/pages/settings/administration/projectsManagement/AvailableModelsSection.tsx:57-152. rationale: Re-verified all 20 findings from code-review-final.json (decision: request-changes, confidence: low, which the artifact itself attributed to an exhausted review budget and uncompleted lenses) directly against the current branch source. Every claimed line number was stale (several pointed past end-of-file, e.g. line 5452 in a 57-line file), confirming the hallucination pattern the task flagged. After reading each target file in full and tracing the described logic by name: 14 findings (CR-001, CR-002, CR-003, CR-004, CR-006, CR-007, CR-008, CR-009, CR-010, CR-011, CR-013, CR-014, CR-017, CR-018) do not reproduce — the described code either already has the guard/handling claimed missing, or (CR-006/007/008/009/010) targets ProjectModelsSection.tsx, a component that is not imported or rendered anywhere in the app and has been superseded by AvailableModelsSection.tsx, which is the component actually wired into ProjectDetailsPage.tsx. The remaining 6 (CR-005, CR-012, CR-015, CR-016, CR-019, CR-020) are interpretive/product-ambiguity concerns where the current code already has a sane, consistent, defensible behavior (e.g. null vs [] for allowed_models, missing projectId meaning 'unrestricted'); no new API contract or behavior was invented to resolve them, per the task's constraint. No source edits were made because no genuine, currently-reproducible defect was found. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and `npx eslint` on all 10 files named across the 20 findings both ran clean. Separately, the standards_review commit-format blocker is corrected: the branch's 14 commits mostly lack any EPMCDME- prefix (worse than the original '5 of 13 wrong format' claim), but .ai-run/guides/standards/git-workflow.md confirms this repo squash-merges feature branches, so only the single squash-merge commit at merge time must match 'EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence' — intermediate commit wording on this branch is not a CI/merge blocker. No remaining unresolved real defects; decision is approve.
